session_covered: European session of Thursday 26 November; US markets closed for Thanksgiving (US figures are Wednesday 25 November closes)
intro: Wall Street was closed on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving, so there was no US session overnight; US figures below are the last closes (Wednesday 25 November). Europe and commodities did trade. This is a delayed, second-attempt brief: the SPI 200 futures direction, VIX and spot gold could not be reliably verified and are marked "not available".
footnotes: US index and 10-year yield levels are Wednesday 25 November closes (S&P 500 -0.25%, NASDAQ -0.62%, Dow +0.33%, 10-year about -6bp); US equity and bond markets did not trade Thursday.
VIX: sources conflicted (FNArena 28.08 at Wednesday's close vs a Yahoo Finance print of 26.80 on a holiday), so it is not available.
Gold: Trading Economics showed US$3,567/oz down 0.6% while Yahoo gold futures showed US$3,593/oz up 0.8%; direction unresolved, so not available.
Iron ore is the 25 November print (no later one found). AUD/USD, Brent and iron ore are CFD-based reference prices (Trading Economics); Brent +1.38% is for Thursday's trade.

setup.summary: The overnight direction of SPI 200 futures is not available: quotes found were undated or stale (Investing.com Dec contract 8,791, +0.71% vs a previous settle of 8,729, which appears to be Thursday's day-session close; TradingView 8,794, +0.22% with "No trades"), and no 27 November market wrap was published when checked. An implied ASX 200 open is therefore not available. For reference, the last day-session futures level was about 8,791. The ASX 200 closed Thursday at about 8,764, up 0.82% (Trading Economics; 8,692.4 prior close), as European shares rallied strongly.

local_events: No scheduled Australian data releases, RBA speeches or notable earnings could be confirmed from the sources checked; consult the ASX and ABS calendars.
what_moved: With Wall Street shut for Thanksgiving, Europe led: the DAX rose 2.08%, the FTSE 100 1.75%, the Euro Stoxx 50 2.18% and the STOXX Europe 600 1.75% (Trading Economics, CFD-based), a rebound after Wednesday's volatile US session in which the Nasdaq was down as much as 4.6% intraday before recovering. Brent rose about 1.4% to US$95.91/bbl. S&P 500 sector moves are not available as there was no US session.

news.headline: Wall Street closed for Thanksgiving
news.summary: US equity and bond markets were shut Thursday; the last readings are Wednesday's, when the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 after a sharp intraday sell-off and late rebound.

news.headline: Hot US inflation keeps Fed hike in view
news.summary: October PCE rose 0.3% m/m for both headline and core (3.8% and 3.3% y/y), and markets price about a 95% chance of a 25bp Fed hike at the 8–9 December meeting.

news.headline: US growth revised higher
news.summary: Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualised.

news.headline: New tariffs and AI-credit worries weighed on Wednesday
news.summary: New "deal rate" tariffs on 14 economies and concerns over AI-linked borrowing costs (credit insurance on CoreWeave and Oracle debt has more than doubled in six months) drove the intraday sell-off.

news.headline: Australian CPI hotter than forecast
news.summary: October CPI ran at 4.9% y/y, with trimmed mean up 0.47% m/m (3.8% y/y); the RBA is expected to stay on hold.

news.headline: European shares rally strongly
news.summary: The DAX gained 2.08% and the FTSE 100 1.75% on Thursday.

news.headline: ASX 200 closes higher; AUD near lows
news.summary: The ASX 200 rose about 0.8% to roughly 8,764 on Thursday, while AUD/USD edged up 0.11% to US$0.6635 after hitting a 51-week low on Wednesday.

news.headline: Brent climbs
news.summary: Brent crude rose about 1.4% to US$95.91/bbl on Thursday, following a 4.3% jump on Wednesday.

coming_up: Wall Street trades a shortened session on Friday 27 November (US time) after the holiday. The next major scheduled event confirmed in the sources is the US Federal Reserve meeting on 8–9 December.
